content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To move to ohio, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Research neighborhoods in Columbus and Cleveland (3 days)
Step 2. Schedule a walkthrough with a real estate agent (1 hour)
Step 3. Hire a long-distance moving company (2 hours)
Step 4. Create a comprehensive moving budget (4 hours)
Step 5. Transfer car insurance to an Ohio-based policy (30 minutes)
Step 6. Pack the kitchen and dining room items (1 day)
Step 7. Set up electricity and water accounts in the new house (1 hour)
Step 8. Confirm the move-in date with the landlord (15 minutes)
Step 9. Purchase heavy-duty moving boxes and tape (1 hour)
Step 10. Clean the current apartment to get the deposit back (6 hours)
Step 11. Forward mail via the Postal Service website (15 minutes)
Step 12. Submit a formal resignation at your current job (2 weeks)
Step 13. Apply for a new apartment lease or mortgage (5 days)
Step 14. Request medical records from your local doctor (1 week)
Step 15. Save money for the security deposit (3 months)
Step 16. Update your resume for the Ohio job market (3 hours)
Step 17. Notify your bank of your change of address (20 minutes)
Step 18. Sell unwanted furniture on an online marketplace (4 days)
Step 19. Register to vote in the new county (10 minutes)
Step 20. Change the address on your Amazon and subscription accounts (45 minutes)
Step 21. Cancel local gym memberships and club subscriptions (30 minutes)
Step 22. Browse job listings in the Ohio area (2 days)
Step 23. Sort through the garage and attic (5 hours)
Step 24. Collect dental and vision records (2 days)
Step 25. Pack the bedroom and bathroom essentials (8 hours)
Step 26. Update the billing address for credit cards (30 minutes)
Step 27. Request time off for the actual moving week (10 minutes)
Step 28. Get a formal credit check for the housing application (1 day)
Step 29. Get a physical exam before leaving your current doctor (1 hour)
Step 30. Research local schools and districts (1 week)
Step 31. Research the cost of living in various Ohio cities (4 hours)
Step 32. Secure professional character references (3 days)
Step 33. Rent a moving truck or trailer (2 hours)
Step 34. Donate old clothes to a local charity (3 hours)
Step 35. Attend virtual job interviews (4 hours)
Step 36. Pick up prescription refills for the transition (30 minutes)
Step 37. Calculate the estimated gas and travel costs (2 hours)
Step 38. Request a final reading of current utilities (20 minutes)
Step 39. Pack the car with suitcases and valuables (2 hours)
Step 40. Drive to the new residence in Ohio (10 hours)
